derivation_notes: The parent assumed the contrast-saturation coefficient is constant across absolute temperature level. Here the nonlinear transfer denominator is re-derived so its saturation strength is multiplicatively modulated by the pair mean temperature, representing temperature-dependent interfacial transport nonlinearity while preserving antisymmetric, energy-conserving exchange.
change_summary: The transport law itself, not only the conductance state target, now depends on mean temperature. This changes the curvature of dT_A_dt versus temperature contrast at fixed effective_conductance, allowing hotter and cooler pairs to saturate at different contrast scales.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The coefficient setting departure from linear-response transport is constant over the full temperature range and does not vary with the pair mean temperature.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Temperature-dependent interfacial transport nonlinearity: phonon/contact or radiative-mixed transfer can shift the onset of sublinear contrast response with absolute temperature level.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Setting conductance_temp_coeff = 0 removes the mean-temperature modulation of the saturation law and recovers the parent target expression.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed effective_conductance, the target depends on temperature contrast only through an odd flux divided by 1 + contrast_nonlinearity_coeff*(T_B - T_A)**2, so the mean temperature affects dT_A_dt only as a multiplicative gain through the conductance state target.
response_change.child_relation: Retain antisymmetric exchange but let the transport nonlinearity itself depend on the pair mean temperature, so the contrast-response curvature of dT_A_dt changes with both T_B - T_A and (T_A + T_B)/2 rather than being a single shared contrast-saturation shape scaled by conductance alone.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with similar instantaneous contrast but different pair mean temperatures, the normalized cooling rate dT_A_dt/(T_B-T_A) bends differently with contrast; hotter pairs can show earlier or later sublinear saturation than cooler pairs, not just a uniform rescaling.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the admissible experiment spans a non-negligible mean-temperature range such that |conductance_temp_coeff*(T_A + T_B)/2| is not tiny, and when the contrast is large enough that contrast_nonlinearity_coeff*(T_B - T_A)^2 is O(1) over part of the trajectory.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying mean temperature mainly changes overall exchange speed through conductance. In holdout, with larger simultaneous contrast and shifted mean temperature, the same mechanism also changes the curvature of the contrast-response, revealing a non-separable mean-temperature-by-contrast interaction.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the mean-temperature dependence of the contrast-saturation law to zero, so the denominator returns to 1 + contrast_nonlinearity_coeff*(T_B - T_A)^2 and only the conductance state carries mean-temperature dependence.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: mean-temperature modulation of nonlinear inter-body heat-transfer saturation
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Temperature-dependent interfacial transport nonlinearity: phonon/contact or radiative-mixed transfer can make the onset of sublinear contrast response shift with the absolute temperature level even while exchange remains antisymmetric and energy conserving.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because mean temperature now changes the denominator's contrast curvature, creating a non-separable interaction between average temperature and contrast rather than a simple gain rescaling of the same contrast-response shape.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The coefficient setting departure from linear-response transport is constant over the full temperature range and does not vary with the pair mean temperature.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The contrast-saturation strength is modulated by the pair mean temperature, shifting the onset of sublinear transfer with absolute temperature level.
evolution_contract.after_fragment: effective_conductance*(T_B - T_A)/(heat_capacity_A*(1 + contrast_nonlinearity_coeff*(1 + conductance_temp_coeff*(T_A + T_B)/2)*(T_B - T_A)**2))
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Setting conductance_temp_coeff = 0 in the target law recovers the parent expression exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compare trajectory segments where effective_conductance and |T_B - T_A| are similar but (T_A + T_B)/2 differs within the admissible range. The parent predicts the same normalized contrast curvature up to amplitude scaling, whereas the child predicts different bending of dT_A_dt versus contrast because the saturation denominator itself changes with mean temperature.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both earlier saturation at one mean temperature and later saturation at another when effective_conductance is supplied, because the parent target mapping has one global contrast-saturation scale and mean temperature enters only through multiplicative conductance. Refitting contrast_nonlinearity_coeff or conductance_temp_coeff merely rescales one shared curve; it cannot make the curve shape conditional on mean temperature across the same dataset.

evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the mean-temperature dependence of the contrast-saturation law to zero, so the denominator returns to 1 + contrast_nonlinearity_coeff*(T_B - T_A)^2 and only the conductance state carries mean-temperature dependence.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes a single fixed contrast-saturation scale for nonlinear heat transfer, independent of the absolute temperature level of the two bodies.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The coefficient setting departure from linear-response transport is constant over the full temperature range and does not vary with the pair mean temperature.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Temperature-dependent interfacial transport nonlinearity: phonon/contact or radiative-mixed transfer can make the onset of sublinear contrast response shift with the absolute temperature level even while exchange remains antisymmetric and energy conserving.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's separability between mean-temperature effects and contrast-saturation effects. In the parent, if effective_conductance is observed, the scored target mapping from supplied states to dT_A_dt has one shared contrast curvature set only by contrast_nonlinearity_coeff; changing mean temperature changes amplitude through effective_conductance but not the shape of rate-versus-contrast. Hold heat capacities fixed and compare portions of trajectories with similar instantaneous |T_B-T_A| but different (T_A+T_B)/2, reachable because the bodies cool/warm toward equilibrium while the conductance state also evolves. The child would allow the saturation scale itself to shift with mean temperature, changing the local slope and curvature of dT_A_dt versus contrast at equal effective_conductance. A single refit of the parent cannot reproduce both earlier saturation at one mean temperature and later saturation at another, because its denominator uses one global contrast scale and its mean-temperature influence is only a multiplicative conductance factor. This refinement remains admissible because it preserves antisymmetric exchange and can be implemented without adding a new state; limitation: if the sampled temperature range is too narrow or contrasts remain very small, the effect is weak and may collapse back to the parent.

scenario_text: Two finite thermal bodies begin at independently specified uniform temperatures and exchange heat only with each other. Their heat capacities and mutual thermal conductance are fixed, and the pair is isolated from the surroundings. The target is the instantaneous rate of change of the first body's temperature while both temperatures are evolved jointly. Linear transport driven by the temperature difference causes monotonic equilibration with an exponentially decaying temperature contrast.
